submission.reasoning: On sysmonlinux-tcontreras-attack-range-643, user ubuntu wrote evil_preload.c and myfopen.c (an fopen hook used for LD_PRELOAD library hijacking, T1574.006). At 11:48:09 they renamed evil_preload.c to prog.c, and at 11:48:17 they compiled it with gcc into /home/ubuntu/prog. Next they created dll_hook.sh and run_hook.sh, set both to chmod 777, and ran 'sudo ./run_hook.sh'. That ran sh ./run_hook.sh as root, which ran sh ./dll_hook.sh (proc-b2aef95380), which ran ./prog as root (proc-c4f0eb4556) at 11:50:17. The user then started building a second hook tool (run_dllhook.c). This is a deliberate library-hijack and privilege-execution sequence, not ordinary development or admin work. I did not confirm the file id behind the dash process's executed_file edge; it is most likely /bin/dash, so it is not listed for deletion.
